To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1. Pancreatectomy causes a severe impairment of the cell-mediated immune response, while humoral immunity is unaffected.
the cell-mediated immune system is severely depressed by diabetes, but not the humoral immune system.

(i) the immunological alterations induced by insulin deprivation in the experimental model of diabetes in rats are mainly restricted to cell-mediated immune responses, and (ii) these alterations are prevented by the daily administration of insulin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of the effect of diabetes on the humoral and cell mediated immune response.
the study of immunological abnormalities in diabetes and their correction with insulin therapy.
the study of the effects of diabetes on the immune system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in the rat diabetes is a disease characterized by a selective depression of cell-mediated immune responses.
the immune system in diabetes is not globally impaired, but only the T-cell mediated immune responses are depressed.
the immunological alterations observed in diabetic rats are due to a selective and differential effect of the insulin-deprived condition on the different lymphoid cell subpopulations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
diabetes is associated with an impairment of cell-mediated immune functions, while antibody production is not significantly affected.

the insulin-dependent immune system is not the whole lymphoid apparatus, but only a part of it, namely the cell-mediated immune apparatus, and that the humoral immune apparatus is independent of insulin.
diabetes mellitus is associated with an immunodepression of cell-mediated immune responses, but not with humoral immune responses, in the rat.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immune system in diabetes patients can be affected by insulin deprivation, and that the effects are more severe in cell-mediated immunity than in antibody production.
insulin deficiency has a differential effect on the immune response.
the immunological system is very sensitive to the presence of insulin and that the insulin-dependent immune alterations can be reversed by insulin treatment.
